clue.text: Electronic fault restricting new display

indicators.note: to restrict something is to hem it in, so the first pair of words wraps around the next

blocks.note: E is the standard abbreviation for electronic
a vice is a moral failing or fault
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A broken electronic gadget, with a fault that stops a new screen from showing anything.
explanation.walkthrough: E and VICE run together as a single outer word, EVICE, which holds the N: E-VI(N)CE.
explanation.definitionFit: To evince a feeling is to show it plainly, so both verbs mean making something visible.

clue.text: Leaf vegetable? Need, in a stew, about four

indicators.note: being in a stew means being agitated and mixed up, so the letters are jumbled
about means going around, so the jumbled letters surround the Roman numeral

blocks.note: the letters to be jumbled
the Roman numeral for four

explanation.surface: A cook who needs a leafy vegetable for a stew, about four of them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a stew' looks like cooking, which suits the vegetable, but it is the jumble signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Endive is a salad plant eaten for its leaves; the question mark admits that 'leaf vegetable' is a loose description.

clue.text: Vignette, proper text with odd parts missing, read

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters are dropped, leaving only the even ones

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth letters and so on, counted straight through the three words

explanation.surface: An editor reading a short sketch whose proper text has bits missing.
explanation.walkthrough: Count through vignette, proper and text as one run of letters, keeping every even-numbered one.
explanation.definitionFit: To read a situation is to understand or construe its meaning, the sense of interpret.

clue.text: Beginnings of markings usually in curve upward in skull

indicators.note: beginnings asks for the opening letter of each of the next two words
in a down clue going upward means reading the assembled letters from bottom to top

blocks.note: first letters of these two words
taken as written
an arc is a curve

explanation.surface: Skull markings that typically curve upward, as an anatomist might note.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'in' looks like a container signal but supplies its own letters; the whole string is then read upward.
explanation.definitionFit: The cranium is the part of the skeleton enclosing the brain, and in loose use the whole skull.

clue.text: Old bottles, emptied and preserved, hidden

indicators.note: a word that is emptied loses all its inside letters and keeps only its two ends

blocks.note: O is the usual abbreviation for old
just the first and last letters of this word
meat or fish that is preserved by salting or smoking is cured

explanation.surface: Old bottles, drained and then pickled, have been put away out of sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old bottles' looks like an old object holding something, but here 'bottles' is not a container signal: it is just a word whose ends are kept.
explanation.definitionFit: Something obscured is concealed or made hard to see, which is the same as being kept out of view.

clue.text: Bird found around rocky crag, lone duck

indicators.note: rocky means unsteady and shaken, so the letters that follow are shaken into a new order
around means surrounding, so the first word goes around the jumbled letters

blocks.note: to found something is to base it, as in found a theory on evidence
letters to be jumbled
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so O

explanation.surface: A lone duck is spotted near a rocky crag by a birdwatcher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duck' looks like the bird the clue is about, but it is a cricket zero, O, which joins the jumble. A duck in cricket is a batter's score of nought.
explanation.definitionFit: The barnacle goose is a black-and-white Arctic goose that winters on the coasts of north-west Europe, so it is a bird.

clue.text: Contrast in heart broken by politician, heart of oak

indicators.note: something broken by another thing is split open with that thing put into the gap
heart of means the central letter of the word that follows

blocks.note: the core of something is its heart
an MP is a Member of Parliament
the middle letter of this three-letter word

explanation.surface: A politician cuts into the heart of the matter, as if splitting the heart of an oak.
explanation.walkthrough: Two different 'heart's do two jobs here: the first is a synonym, the second asks for a middle letter. 'In' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To contrast two things is to set them side by side to show differences, which is one way to compare them.

clue.text: Speaker's beginning course

indicators.note: a speaker's version is how something is said, so the next word is heard rather than read

blocks.note: the root of something is its beginning or origin; the answer can be said the same way

explanation.surface: A speaker opens a talk at the start of a course of lectures.
explanation.walkthrough: This depends on saying the answer to rhyme with 'boot', the usual British pronunciation.
explanation.definitionFit: A route is a course or way taken to get from one place to another.

clue.text: Pleasant fantasy story finally penned by father on quantity of paper

indicators.note: finally asks for only the last letter of the word before it
something penned is shut in a pen, so the single letter goes inside the word for a parent
in a down clue, on means placed above, so the parent piece comes first

blocks.note: an everyday word for father
the final letter of this word
a ream is a fixed quantity of paper, traditionally 500 sheets

explanation.surface: A father writes a happy fantasy story at the end of a big stack of paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penned' looks like writing, which suits the father telling a story, but it means enclosed.
explanation.definitionFit: A daydream is a pleasant fantasy indulged in while awake, a reverie of wishful thinking.

clue.text: Revolutionary nonsense transported critic

indicators.note: something revolutionary turns right round, so the words after it are read from the end back to the start

blocks.note: rot is rubbish or nonsense
goods that are carted are transported

explanation.surface: A newspaper report: radical nonsense has carried away a reviewer.
explanation.walkthrough: ROT and CARTED, read together right to left, give DETRACTOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A detractor disparages or runs down something, which is what a hostile critic does.

clue.text: Agitators break rule most recklessly

indicators.note: done recklessly means done wildly and carelessly, so the letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Protesters flout the rules more wildly than anyone.
explanation.definitionFit: Troublemakers stir up unrest and cause disturbances, just as agitators provoke people to protest.

clue.text: Shy maiden, poor, left out

indicators.note: out says the letter just named is taken away and missing from the word

blocks.note: M is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for a maiden over
lousy means very poor in quality
L is the abbreviation for left; this is the letter dropped

explanation.surface: A timid young woman, impoverished and left out of things.
explanation.walkthrough: A maiden is a cricket over with no runs, so it is M. Take the L out of LOUSY and put M in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Mousy describes a quiet, timid person who keeps in the background, like a shy little mouse.

clue.text: Rig vote designed to cause feeling of instability

indicators.note: designed means put together to a new plan, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An election fix, cooked up to unsettle the political scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Vertigo is a dizzy sensation of spinning or losing balance, a physical sense of being unsteady.

clue.text: Inexpert, united, right behind a friend

indicators.note: behind places the first two letters after the next pair in the finished word

blocks.note: taken as written
a mate is a friend
U is the abbreviation for United, as in football club names
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Someone clumsy, backed up by a pal, gets support from behind.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective, amateur means unskilled or unprofessional, so an amateur job is an inexpert one.

clue.text: Important dancer having cracked rib, in alarm, pale

indicators.note: something cracked is broken apart, so these letters break up and re-form

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A leading dancer has broken a rib and gone white with fright.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'in' is part of the fodder, not a container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The prima ballerina is the principal female dancer of a ballet company, its most senior and important performer.

clue.text: Run up with documents from debtors? Not interested

blocks.note: to run up a debt is to incur it
an IOU is a signed note acknowledging a debt

explanation.surface: Someone running up debts and holding IOUs, but not caring about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run up' looks like the up-means-reverse signal of a down clue, but it is just the phrase for running up a bill.
explanation.definitionFit: Incurious describes a person lacking curiosity, who shows no desire to know or find out more.

clue.text: Satisfactorily located in row, good home

indicators.note: located in says the first word sits inside the noise word

blocks.note: a din is a loud noise, a row
doing something well is doing it satisfactorily
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A nice place to live, conveniently sited in a terrace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' suggests a row of houses, fitting home, but it is the noisy kind of row.
explanation.definitionFit: A dwelling is a house or other place where someone lives, a formal word for a residence.

clue.text: Sense retreat, for example, brought about by champion defending north vigorously

indicators.note: brought about is a sailing phrase for turning a ship round, so the short abbreviation faces the other way
to defend something is to surround and guard it, so one piece sits inside another

blocks.note: wit is good sense or intelligence
a haven is a place of refuge or retreat
e.g. abbreviates exempli gratia, for example
an ace is an expert or champion
N is the abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: A war report: a champion fighting hard to hold the north, with good sense and a place to fall back to.
explanation.walkthrough: WIT + HAVEN + GE, then ACE holding N: WIT-HAVEN-GE-A(N)CE.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom with a vengeance means forcefully or to an extreme degree, i.e. done with great energy.

clue.text: Gang ahead after a scrap

indicators.note: after puts the group and the forward word behind the single letter

blocks.note: taken as written
a band is a group or gang
on means forward, ahead, as in go on

explanation.surface: A gang gets in front of others after a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrap' suggests a fight, which suits the gang, but it is the verb meaning give up.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrap a plan is to drop or give it up, which is to abandon it.

clue.text: Top star is in remake

indicators.note: in places the two-letter word inside the verb that follows

blocks.note: taken as written
to remake something is to alter it

explanation.surface: A big celebrity is cast in a film remake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Remake' reads like a film, but here it is the verb meaning change.
explanation.definitionFit: An A-lister is a celebrity on the A-list, the top tier of the most famous people.

clue.text: Batting, lean and mean

blocks.note: in cricket the side batting is in
to lean towards something is to tend towards it

explanation.surface: A cricketer at the crease who is thin and nasty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lean and mean' looks like two adjectives describing a player, but lean is a verb and mean is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To mean to do something is to have it as a purpose, the verb sense of intend.

clue.text: Monk admitting naughty dance

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so the first word takes the next one inside it

blocks.note: a lama is a Buddhist monk in Tibet
a naughty child is a bad one

explanation.surface: A holy man lets in someone who does a racy dance.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tibetan monk is the usual crossword monk, alongside the abbreviation for a friar.
explanation.definitionFit: The lambada is a fast, sensual Brazilian partner dance popular around 1990.

clue.text: Type of whisky available initially in country

indicators.note: initially asks for just the first letter of the word before it

blocks.note: malt whisky is made from malted barley
the opening letter of this word

explanation.surface: A kind of whisky can be bought at first in a particular country.
explanation.definitionFit: Malta is an island nation in the Mediterranean, south of Sicily, so it is a country.

clue.text: Letter, second sent round by Conservative in club

indicators.note: sent round means turned to face the other way, so the short word is read backwards
in places the party abbreviation inside the golf word

blocks.note: a mo is a moment, a second
C is the abbreviation for Conservative
an iron is a type of golf club

explanation.surface: A letter is posted round, delivered by a Tory member of a club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letter' and 'sent round' suggest the post, but the letter is from the Greek alphabet, and the club is for golf.
explanation.definitionFit: Omicron is the fifteenth character of the Greek alphabet, so it is a letter.

clue.text: One day, provoked, did nothing

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
D is the abbreviation for day
led in the sense of drew on or induced, as in led someone to act

explanation.surface: Someone goaded one day, but stayed passive and did not respond.
explanation.definitionFit: To idle is to pass time lazily without working, so having idled means having been inactive.

clue.text: Conductor using baton with energy after return

indicators.note: after places the stick and the physics symbol behind the voting word

blocks.note: to return a candidate to parliament is to elect them
a baton is a short rod or stick
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: An orchestra conductor waves the baton energetically after coming back on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a music conductor; the definition means an electrical one.
explanation.definitionFit: An electrode is a terminal through which electric current passes into or out of a circuit, a kind of electrical conductor.

clue.text: Aim to go back aboard schooner perhaps for pleasure

indicators.note: going back means travelling in the opposite direction, so the word is read from its end
aboard means on board, held inside a vessel, so one word sits in the other

blocks.note: an end is a goal or aim
a schooner is a large glass for sherry or beer, so it is an example of one

explanation.surface: Sailing back aboard a schooner purely for the fun of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Schooner' suggests a sailing ship, which 'aboard' supports, but here it is a big drinking glass, a British and Australian measure for sherry or beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Gladness is a state of being happy or pleased, a close synonym of pleasure as a feeling.

clue.text: Blunder, as edited, partly rubbed out

indicators.note: partly says only a part of the run of words is wanted, sitting inside them

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word, the whole second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A mistake that, once edited, was partly deleted.
explanation.definitionFit: Erased means wiped away or removed, as pencil marks are when rubbed out with an eraser.
